at.step: The W3C Trace Context specification and the tracing crate's own documentation state this directly: a trace id and a parent id are real, specific byte values joined into one real, specified format; a span or event's own fields are key-value data, not unstructured text. Do this topic's own three measured comparisons model exactly the rule both sources describe?

items.item: All three claims are measured by parsing a real binary's own stdout for values it itself computed and printed, never by re-deriving a value the Python harness could compute independently; the harness only checks what the real Rust program already asserted about itself.

items.item: The structured-field total is recovered by a real tracing_subscriber::Layer visiting each event's own typed attempt field directly, through tracing::field::Visit, never by formatting the event into text first and then re-parsing that text.

items.item: The formatted-message-only total is deliberately computed by regex-extracting the first run of digits out of each event's own rendered message text, which is exactly the lossy, informal recovery a person reading a log file by eye would otherwise have to do.

at.step: The identical total is attempted again, this time recovered only from each event's own rendered, formatted message, by pulling out the first run of digits found in it. Does that give the identical, correct total too?

items.item: One of the three real messages is deliberately worded as 'third attempt now running' rather than 'attempt 3 now running', so the digit-based text recovery genuinely fails to find any number in it at all, which is the real, specific mechanism behind the wrong total rather than a contrived or hypothetical one.

items.item: request_id, tenant, shard, partition, operation, and queue depth are named directly in Internals rather than measured in code, since this topic's own crate needs only one real structured field, attempt, to demonstrate the identical property the syllabus names for all of them: a typed field survives being queried where the same value in a sentence does not.

tracing-opentelemetry, a real OTLP collector, and a real Kafka broker are named in In production rather than measured, since none of the three is reachable from this sandboxed container; this topic's own code instead implements and measures the real traceparent header format directly, which is the part of the propagation mechanism that survives the network.

The W3C Trace Context specification and the tracing crate's own field documentation are two genuinely separate sources describing two genuinely different real mechanisms (a wire header format, and an in-process typed field), giving this topic two sources rather than multiple quotes drawn from a single page.
